items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: And there was another guy I had mentioned -- Henry Bachelor, piano player. See, we had a whole gang of piano players around there and they all were working, too.

ctx.x: Then you come up around there?

Oh, yeah. I was born in Boston. Church and Melrose. And there was another guy I had mentioned -- Henry Bachelor, piano player. See, we had a whole gang of piano players around there and they all were working, too. All had a government job, and we used to get jobs. I used to go down to the St. Jordan marsh there and go up in the man's office and sit down and talk with him, and get -- about a job. We'd talk over all the conditions and everything.

And I was playing down on Beech Street, and a Harvard student came in one night and he says, 'hey, how much you charge to play down in Worcester?' I said, '$500,' just like that, see. Now, I didn't know -- I thought he was kidding, see, so I said $500. I had four men there. So about a couple of weeks later, this guy came in, hey, remember what we was talking about? I said, oh, yeah. He said, well, the job is on such-and-such a day.
